title: orders.order-confirmed.v1
description: A draft became a confirmed order, and the rest of the shop starts from here: Custody allocates a barcode identity per garment inside the same transaction (INV-ORD-01, through the confirmation-participant hook rather than through this event), Billing #42 converts an order to an invoice, Reporting #45 counts a new order into the pipeline, and Notifications tells the customer. The payload carries no totals and none of the three configuration version identifiers — the price snapshot is Confidential and no subscriber is approved for it — no notes (free text a member of staff typed), no priority (named as a column in module-ownership section 5.5 but given no vocabulary by any document) and no actor, on the same line customers.customer-merged.v1 takes.
$comment: additionalProperties is true on purpose. conventions.md section 5.5 permits additive changes within a major version, so a subscriber must tolerate a field it has not seen; a closed schema would make every such addition breaking. required lists the fields present when v1 was published — a field added within v1 is optional forever, because a dead-lettered message replayed later carries the payload as it was written.

eventId.description: Identity of this occurrence. Delivery is at least once; consumers de-duplicate on it.

occurredAt.description: When the order was confirmed, in UTC.

aggregateId.description: The order. Every order-scoped event that follows — a revision, a cancellation — is ordered against it.

organisationId.description: The organisation the order belongs to.

branchId.description: The branch that took the order. Never null: branch scope is evaluated and never inferred, and the branch is the sequence key the order number came from.

customerId.description: The customer the order is for. An identifier and nothing more. Reporting #45 counts new against repeat from it, and Billing #42 starts its bill-to lookup here through ICustomerSnapshotQuery.

orderNumber.description: The human reference, O-<branch>-<FY>-000001 (docs/architecture/conventions.md section 3.2). A label a person quotes, never a lookup key.

orderDraftId.description: The draft that was confirmed. It is how an idempotent confirmation recognises a retry: the same draft confirmed twice is one order, not two.

estimateId.description: The estimate this order was converted from, or null where the counter confirmed without quoting first. Plan #42 carries it as the invoice's source estimate.

dueDate.description: The order's promised date, branch-local (docs/architecture/conventions.md section 2.2). A garment may promise its own, which is the date a workshop queue is ordered by.

garmentJobCount.description: How many garments the order was confirmed with, and so how many orders.garment-job-created.v1 events accompany this one. Load-bearing: those events carry the garment as their aggregate, so per-aggregate ordering cannot tell a consumer the set is complete. At least one — an order with no garment is refused.

revisionNumber.description: The revision this confirmation states the order at. One at first confirmation, and higher where the event is republished after a revision. Present at v1 precisely so a republication needs no new major.

schemaVersion.description: The payload's major version. Agrees with the .v suffix of eventType.
